stem: A galvanic cell configuration corresponding to the dissolution of the sparingly soluble salt $\text{Ag}_x\text{Cl}_y$ (where $x = 1$ and $y = 1$ in $\text{A}_x\text{B}_y$) has a standard EMF of the cell whose net reaction is the dissolution equal to $-0.577\text{ V}$, with $1$ electron transferred ($n = 1$). In a separate experiment at $298\text{ K}$, a volume of the cation solution of $100.0\text{ mL}$ of $\text{Ag}^+$ with a concentration of the cation solution before mixing of $4\text{e-}05\text{ mol L}^{-1}$ is mixed with a volume of the anion solution of $100.0\text{ mL}$ of $\text{Cl}^-$ with a concentration of the anion solution before mixing of $3\text{e-}05\text{ mol L}^{-1}$. Given that $2.303RT/F = 0.0591\text{ V}$ at $298\text{ K}$, determine whether a precipitate forms.

For the gas-phase dissociation reaction PCl5(g) ⇌ PCl3(g) + Cl2(g), the standard Gibbs energy change is 5.0 kJ mol⁻¹ at temperature T₁ = 400.0 K. The equilibrium constant K at T₂ = 500.0 K is 4.5. Assuming the standard enthalpy change ΔH° and standard entropy change are constant over this temperature range, and the standard entropy change of the reaction is 120.0 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ (having the same sign as ΔH°), calculate the temperature at which ΔG = 0 in K.
(Given: R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)

The thermal decomposition of dinitrogen pentoxide (N2O5) in a closed vessel follows first-order kinetics. At 300.0 K, an initial concentration of 0.5 mol L⁻¹ decreases to a concentration of 0.2 mol L⁻¹ after a time elapsed of 1800.0 s. When the reaction is carried out at temperature 320.0 K, the rate constant is 0.00624 s⁻¹. Given that R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, calculate the fraction of molecules with energy ≥ E_a at temperature 600.0 K.

The first-order gas-phase thermal decomposition of di-tert-butyl peroxide into acetone and ethane is monitored in a closed vessel. At a temperature of 410.0 K, the initial concentration of di-tert-butyl peroxide is 0.8 mol L⁻¹, which decreases to a concentration of 0.2 mol L⁻¹ after a time elapsed of 2400.0 s. When the reaction is carried out at a temperature of 430.0 K, the rate constant is 0.00479 s⁻¹. Given R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, determine the fraction of molecules with energy ≥ E_a at a temperature of 750.0 K.

The first-order gas-phase thermal decomposition of di-tert-butyl peroxide into acetone and ethane is carried out in a closed vessel at constant volume. At a temperature of 500.0 K, the initial concentration of 0.04 mol L⁻¹ decreases to a concentration of 0.01 mol L⁻¹ after a time elapsed of 1800.0 s. At a temperature of 520.0 K, the decomposition exhibits a rate constant of 0.00281 s⁻¹. Given R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, calculate the fraction of molecules with energy ≥ E_a at a temperature of 650.0 K.

The gas-phase thermal decomposition of di-tert-butyl peroxide (DTBP) into ethane and acetone in a rigid vessel follows first-order kinetics. When the reaction is carried out at 430.0 K, the concentration of DTBP decreases from an initial concentration of 0.06 mol L⁻¹ to 0.015 mol L⁻¹ after an elapsed time of 2400.0 s. At 450.0 K, the rate constant of the reaction is 0.00402 s⁻¹.

Given: R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹

Calculate the fraction of molecules with energy ≥ E_a at a temperature of 550.0 K.

An automotive airbag test vessel contains argon gas whose partial volume is 8.4 L under the operational test conditions of 1.25 atm and 320.0 K. Separately, 180.0 g of an aqueous sodium azide (NaN₃) solution having a concentration of 24.5 % w/W is completely evaporated to isolate pure solid NaN₃. This solid is transferred into the vessel and completely decomposed via heating into solid sodium and nitrogen gas. Assuming ideal gas behavior and negligible volume occupied by any condensed phases, calculate the total volume (L) of the inflated bag at the final temperature of 320.0 K and pressure of 1.25 atm. (Given: R = 0.0821 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; atomic masses: Na = 23, N = 14)

A reversible electrochemical cell is set up according to the overall reaction:
$$\mathrm{Zn(s) + 2AgCl(s) \rightarrow ZnCl_2(aq) + 2Ag(s)}$$
where $2$ moles of electrons are transferred per mole of reaction. The standard molar heat capacity difference for the reaction, $\Delta_r C_p = \sum C_p(\text{products}) - \sum C_p(\text{reactants})$, is $-38.5\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$ and remains constant over the temperature range from $T_1 = 298\text{ K}$ to $T_2 = 350\text{ K}$. At temperature $298\text{ K}$, potentiometric characterization yields an EMF of the cell equal to $1.015\text{ V}$, and the temperature coefficient of the electromotive force at constant pressure, $(\partial E/\partial T)_P$, is $-0.000402 \times 10^0\text{ V K}^{-1}$. If the entropy change of the cell reaction at temperature $350\text{ K}$ is $-82.4\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, calculate the Gibbs energy change (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) for the cell reaction at temperature $350\text{ K}$.
(Take $F = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$)

A reversible galvanic cell involves a reaction in which 2 electrons are transferred per mole of reaction. At an initial temperature T₁ = 298 K, the EMF of the cell is measured to be 1.25 V, and its temperature derivative at constant pressure, (∂E/∂T)_P, is 0.00035 × 10⁰ V K⁻¹. The constant-pressure heat capacity difference for the cell reaction is ΔrC_p = ΣC_p(products) − ΣC_p(reactants) = 85.0 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ over the temperature range from temperature T₁ = 298 K to an elevated temperature T₂ = 450 K. If the reaction entropy change at temperature 450 K is 102.6 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, calculate the reaction Gibbs energy change (kJ mol⁻¹) at temperature 450 K. (Take F = 96500 C mol⁻¹)

For the gas-phase reaction 2A + B → 3C + D carried out at 300 K under conditions where reactant B is kept in constant large excess, the initial rate of appearance of product C is monitored across different trials. In the second run, where the initial concentration of A is 0.45 mol L⁻¹ while other concentrations remain unchanged, the initial rate of formation of C is found to be 0.324 mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹. In an initial baseline run with the concentration of A at 0.15 mol L⁻¹, the rate of disappearance of A was measured to be 0.024 mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹. Determine the order of the reaction with respect to reactant A.

For the gas-phase catalytic reaction 3A(g) + B(g) → 2C(g) + D(g), kinetic experiments were performed at a constant temperature with reactant B present in large excess. In Run 1, starting with [A] = 0.16 mol L⁻¹, the initial rate of disappearance of A was observed to be 0.054 mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹. In Run 2, where the initial concentration of A was adjusted to 0.4 mol L⁻¹ with all other concentrations unchanged, the initial rate of formation of C was measured as 0.225 mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹. Determine the order of the reaction with respect to A.

An equimolar gaseous mixture containing methane (molar mass 16.0 g mol⁻¹) and the vapor of an unknown volatile non-electrolyte solute is introduced into a separation apparatus operating over 6 effusion stages. In a separate determination, a solution prepared by dissolving 6.4 g of this solute in 125.0 g of benzene exhibited a freezing point depression of 1.024 K. Given that the cryoscopic constant of benzene is 5.12 K kg mol⁻¹, calculate the overall separation factor for methane relative to the solute vapor achieved across the cascade.

A direct hydrazine–oxygen fuel cell operates reversibly at 298 K according to the overall reaction:
$$\text{N}_2\text{H}_4(\text{aq}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$$
In this cell reaction, the number of electrons transferred per mole of $\text{N}_2\text{H}_4$ consumed is 4, and the cell EMF is maintained at 1.56 V. Determine the maximum useful (non-PV) work obtainable when 0.35 mol of $\text{N}_2\text{H}_4$ is completely consumed.
(Take $F = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$)
Give the answer in kJ.

A fully charged secondary lead-acid storage battery operates reversibly at 298 K according to the overall discharge reaction:
$$\mathrm{Pb(s) + PbO_2(s) + 2H_2SO_4(aq) \rightarrow 2PbSO_4(s) + 2H_2O(l)}$$
For every formula unit of the reaction written above, the number of electrons transferred in the cell reaction is 2. During discharge under standard operational conditions at this temperature, the cell EMF is maintained at 2.05 V. If a continuous discharge process consumes an amount reacting of 0.45 mol of $\mathrm{Pb(s)}$, calculate the maximum useful (non-PV) work obtainable (kJ). [Take $F = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$]
Give the answer in kJ.

A hydrazine–oxygen fuel cell operating in an alkaline medium undergoes complete oxidation of 0.35 mol of hydrazine according to the overall reaction:
$$\mathrm{N_2H_4(aq) + O_2(g) \rightarrow N_2(g) + 2H_2O(l)}$$
The electrochemical process involves 4 electrons transferred in the cell reaction per formula unit of hydrazine consumed. If the fuel cell operates continuously at a steady cell EMF of 1.56 V, calculate the maximum useful (non-PV) work obtainable (kJ) under these conditions.
(Take $F = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$)
Give the answer in kJ.

In a direct methanol fuel cell operating at 298 K, liquid methanol is electrochemically oxidized by oxygen to carbon dioxide and liquid water, involving 6 electrons transferred in the cell reaction per molecule of methanol oxidized. During steady operation, the measured cell EMF is 1.18 V when 0.45 mol of methanol is completely consumed.

Take Faraday constant, F = 96500 C mol⁻¹.

Calculate the magnitude of the maximum useful (non-PV) work obtainable (kJ) from this process under the given operating conditions.
Give the answer in kJ.

In an evacuated container of initial volume 5.0 L maintained at an initial temperature 300.0 K, excess solid ammonium hydrosulfide and excess solid ammonium chloride simultaneously undergo decomposition according to the equilibria: NH₄HS(s) ⇌ NH₃(g) + H₂S(g) with K_p = 0.28 atm², and NH₄Cl(s) ⇌ NH₃(g) + HCl(g) with K_p = 0.21 atm². The resulting gaseous mixture is subsequently transferred to a separate chamber where an amount of ideal gas of 0.284 mol is isolated. This sample, behaving as a diatomic gas, is subjected to a thermodynamic process that brings it to a final temperature of 480.0 K and a final volume of 12.5 L (with the same T and amount for the initial state of the expansion). Taking R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ and assuming ideal behavior, determine the entropy change of the gas (J K⁻¹). Give the answer in J K⁻¹.

A high-pressure chemical reactor operates with gaseous carbon dioxide maintained at a pressure of 75.0 atm and a temperature of 450.0 K. Gaseous carbon dioxide is modeled as a real gas with van der Waals parameters a = 3.64 atm L² mol⁻² and b = 0.0425 L mol⁻¹, having a critical temperature T_c. Calculate the reduced temperature of carbon dioxide in the reactor under these operating conditions. (Given: R = 0.0821 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)

A high-pressure chemical reactor contains ethylene gas maintained at a temperature of 300.0 K and a pressure of 126.8 atm. The gas exhibits non-ideal behavior characterized by the van der Waals constants a = 4.48 atm L² mol⁻² and b = 0.0572 L mol⁻¹. Taking the universal gas constant R = 0.0821 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, determine the reduced pressure of ethylene in this state.

In a supercritical fluid extraction chamber, a sample of xenon gas is maintained at a temperature of 439.8 K and a pressure of 58.4 atm. Assuming xenon obeys the van der Waals equation of state with parameters a = 4.19 atm L² mol⁻² and b = 0.0516 L mol⁻¹, calculate the reduced temperature of the gas corresponding to its critical temperature T_c. (Take R = 0.0821 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)

In a supercritical fluid extraction plant, a reactor containing carbon dioxide operates at a temperature of the gas of 320.0 K and a pressure of the gas of 110.7 atm to decaffeinate green coffee beans. Treating carbon dioxide as a real gas modeled with van der Waals a = 3.65 atm L² mol⁻² and van der Waals b = 0.0428 L mol⁻¹ (with universal gas constant R = 0.0821 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹), evaluate the critical constant P_c to determine the reduced variable, reduced pressure, of the operating gas.

In a thermochemical experiment conducted at constant pressure, an aqueous hydrochloric acid solution is mixed with an aqueous sodium hydroxide solution inside a solution calorimeter. The activation energy of the forward combination of hydronium and hydroxide ions to form liquid water is 12.5 kJ mol⁻¹. The initial temperature of the calorimeter and its contents is 298.15 K. Following complete reaction yielding 0.05 mol of water formed, the final temperature reaches 301.75 K. The heat capacity of the calorimeter (including the resulting solution) is 0.795 kJ K⁻¹. Assuming negligible heat loss to the surroundings, calculate the activation energy of the backward reaction. Give the answer in kJ mol⁻¹.

An analytical chemist prepares a dilute solution by taking 120.0 mL of an aqueous potassium sulfate solution of concentration 1.25 mol L⁻¹ and mixing it thoroughly with 380.0 mL of pure water. The molar mass of the solute is 174.0 g mol⁻¹. The resulting solution has a measured density of 1.042 g mL⁻¹ and exhibits a van 't Hoff factor of 2.7 under these conditions. Given that the depression of freezing point constant of the solvent is 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹, determine the depression of freezing point of the prepared solution. Assume volume additivity upon mixing. Give the answer in K.

An aqueous stock solution of sodium hydrogen sulfate (molar mass of the solute: 120.06 g mol⁻¹) with an initial molarity: 2.4 mol L⁻¹ is measured out at an initial volume of the solution: 75.0 mL. Pure water is added to this sample with a volume of water added: 225.0 mL, yielding a thoroughly mixed solution having a density of the solution: 1.052 g mL⁻¹. In this diluted system, taking into account the secondary equilibrium of the hydrogen sulfate ion, the van 't Hoff factor i (1 for a non-electrolyte): 2.35. For water, the depression of freezing point constant of the solvent: 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹. Calculate the depression of freezing point (K). Give the answer in K.

An aqueous stock solution of sodium hydrogen sulfate (NaHSO4, molar mass of the solute: 120.06 g mol⁻¹) has an initial molarity of 1.5 mol L⁻¹. An initial volume of the solution of 80.0 mL is diluted by mixing with a volume of water added of 320.0 mL (assume volumes are additive). The resulting diluted solution has a density of the solution of 1.028 g mL⁻¹. Under these conditions, secondary dissociation of the hydrogen sulfate ion leads to an effective van 't Hoff factor of 2.181. For water, the depression of freezing point constant of the solvent is 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹. Calculate the depression of freezing point (K) of the diluted solution. Give the answer in K.

An aqueous stock solution of sodium hydrogen sulfate (molar mass of the solute: 120.06 g mol⁻¹) has an initial molarity of 0.75 mol L⁻¹. A 60.0 mL initial volume of the solution is mixed thoroughly with 240.0 mL volume of water added. Cryoscopic analysis of the resulting diluted mixture reveals that the electrolyte displays a van 't Hoff factor i (1 for a non-electrolyte) of 2.25. The density of the solution is 1.012 g mL⁻¹, and the depression of freezing point constant of the solvent is 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹. Determine the depression of freezing point (K). Give the answer in K.

In an experiment, two electrolytic cells containing aqueous solutions of CuSO4 (Cell 1) and AgNO3 (Cell 2) are connected in series. A constant electric current is maintained through the circuit until a total charge of 4825.0 C has passed. In Cell 1, copper ions undergo reduction with 2 electrons per ion discharged, corresponding to a molar mass of 63.55 g mol⁻¹ and an equivalent mass of 31.775 g eq⁻¹ for copper. In Cell 2, silver metal is deposited with an equivalent mass of 107.87 g eq⁻¹. The silver deposited on the cathode is carefully collected, dried, and immersed in a pycnometer, where the volume of the sample is determined to be 0.514 mL. Assuming 100% current efficiency in both cells and taking F = 96500 C mol⁻¹, calculate the density of the deposited silver. Give the answer in g mL⁻¹.

An electrolytic apparatus consists of two voltameters connected in series. Cell 1 contains an acidic solution of chromium(III) sulfate, where the electrodeposition of metallic chromium (molar mass of the substance deposited: 52.0 g mol⁻¹) involves 3 electrons per ion discharged, yielding an equivalent mass of the substance in cell 1: 17.333 g eq⁻¹. Cell 2 contains an aqueous solution of lead(II) nitrate, characterized by an equivalent mass of the substance in cell 2: 103.6 g eq⁻¹. A steady direct current is maintained through the circuit until a total charge passed: 14475.0 C is recorded. Following electrolysis, the coherent deposit of metallic lead harvested from the cathode of Cell 2 is found to have a volume of the sample: 1.37 mL. Take F = 96500 C mol⁻¹. Assuming ideal Faradaic efficiency, calculate the density of the electrodeposited lead. Give the answer in g mL⁻¹.

An electrochemical setup is constructed by connecting two voltameters in series to a constant current source. Cell 1 is charged with an acidic chromium(III) sulfate electrolyte, where cathodic reduction requires 3 electrons per ion discharged to deposit metallic chromium (molar mass 52.0 g mol⁻¹, corresponding to an equivalent mass of 17.333 g eq⁻¹). Cell 2 contains an aqueous lead(II) nitrate bath having an equivalent mass of 103.6 g eq⁻¹ for the metal deposition process. Electrolysis is carried out until a net charge of 14475.0 C is transferred through the circuit. At the end of the run, the dense metallic lead formed on the cathode of Cell 2 is isolated, dried, and determined to occupy a volume of 1.37 mL. Assume ideal 100% Faradaic efficiency across both cells and take F = 96500 C mol⁻¹. Determine the density of the electrodeposited lead. Give the answer in g mL⁻¹.

In an electrogravimetric experiment, two electrolytic cells containing aqueous NiSO4 (cell 1) and aqueous AgNO3 (cell 2) are connected in series. A constant direct current delivers a total charge passed of 19300.0 C through the circuit. In cell 1, nickel is deposited where the molar mass of the substance deposited is 58.69 g mol⁻¹ with 2 electrons per ion discharged, corresponding to an equivalent mass of the substance in cell 1 of 29.345 g eq⁻¹. In cell 2, silver ions are reduced to metallic silver, with an equivalent mass of the substance in cell 2 of 107.87 g eq⁻¹. The metallic silver deposited on the cathode of cell 2 is completely recovered, dried, and immersed in a liquid pycnometer, displacing a volume of the sample of 2.06 mL. Take F = 96500 C mol⁻¹. Determine the density (g mL⁻¹) of the electrodeposited silver. Give the answer in g mL⁻¹.

In an industrial wastewater treatment facility, an electrolytic cell (Cell 1) containing 50000.0 g of wastewater with copper(II) ions at a concentration of 254.16 ppm (by mass) is connected in series with Cell 2 containing an aqueous solution of chromium(III) sulfate. Exhaustive electrolysis is carried out such that all the copper(II) ions in Cell 1 are completely reduced to metallic copper. Under these conditions, the equivalent mass of the substance in cell 1 is 31.77 g eq⁻¹, the equivalent mass of the substance in cell 2 is 17.33 g eq⁻¹, and the molar mass of the compound deposited in Cell 2 is 52.0 g mol⁻¹. Determine the total amount of chromium deposited at the cathode of Cell 2. Give the answer in mol.

An aqueous sample containing an unknown mixture of NaOH and Na2CO3 is titrated with standard hydrochloric acid. Reaching the phenolphthalein end point requires an amount of acid equivalent to 5.105 g of potassium hydrogen phthalate (equivalent mass: 204.2 g eq⁻¹). From this stage, reaching the methyl orange end point requires a further 0.01 eq of HCl. Given that 1 sodium ion is furnished by each formula unit of NaOH, calculate the total number of sodium ions in the mixture that originate strictly from NaOH. Take N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹. Give the answer to 3 significant figures.

An alkaline aqueous mixture containing sodium hydroxide and sodium carbonate is titrated at 298 K. The titration up to the phenolphthalein end point requires the complete addition of a standard solution prepared by dissolving a mass of the substance equal to 2.719 g of pure sulfamic acid (equivalent mass: 97.09 g eq⁻¹) in water. To complete the neutralization of the resulting solution, further titration from the phenolphthalein to the methyl orange end point requires 0.0115 eq of HCl. Assuming each formula unit of NaOH completely dissociates in water to yield 2 ions, calculate the total number of ions furnished by NaOH in the initial mixture. (Take N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹). Give the answer to 3 significant figures.

In a chemical process, 0.45 mol of Fe3O4 is converted into Fe2(SO4)3 according to the conversion Fe3O4 -> Fe2(SO4)3, with complete conservation of Fe. The entire amount of Fe2(SO4)3 produced is then allowed to react with 3.8 mol of NaOH in aqueous solution according to the balanced equation:
Fe2(SO4)3 + 6 NaOH -> 2 Fe(OH)3 + 3 Na2SO4

Give the formula of the limiting reagent.

A 1.2 mol sample of Al(OH)3 is converted into Al2(SO4)3 via the reaction Al(OH)3 -> Al2(SO4)3, with all the Al conserved in the resulting Al2(SO4)3. The entire amount of Al2(SO4)3 obtained is then treated with 4.2 mol of NaOH according to the balanced chemical equation:
Al2(SO4)3 + 8 NaOH -> 2 Na[Al(OH)4] + 3 Na2SO4

Give the formula of the limiting reagent.

In a process, 1.2 mol of Al(OH)3 is converted following the scheme Al(OH)3 -> Al2(SO4)3 with complete conservation of Al. The resulting amount of Al2(SO4)3 is subsequently treated with 4.2 mol of NaOH according to the balanced equation:
Al2(SO4)3 + 8 NaOH -> 2 Na[Al(OH)4] + 3 Na2SO4

Give the formula of the limiting reagent.

In an industrial process, 0.75 mol of Ca3(PO4)2 is treated with carbon and silica according to the reaction:
2 Ca3(PO4)2 + 10 C + 6 SiO2 -> P4 + 6 CaSiO3 + 10 CO

Assuming that all the P atoms from the Ca3(PO4)2 are conserved and converted exclusively into P4, the entire yield of P4 is subsequently reacted with 3.6 mol of Cl2 to synthesize phosphorus pentachloride according to the balanced equation:
P4 + 10 Cl2 -> 4 PCl5

Give the formula of the limiting reagent.

A 2.19 mL sample of pure ethanol is completely oxidised to acetic acid using the unreacted potassium dichromate remaining in an acidic reaction mixture. The reaction mixture was initially prepared by mixing 0.075 mol of potassium dichromate with 0.3 mol of iron(II) sulfate in an acidic medium, where 1 mol of potassium dichromate reacts with 6 mol of iron(II) sulfate. Calculate the density of the ethanol sample.

(Given: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)

Give the answer in g mL⁻¹, to 3 significant figures.

For the gaseous dissociation reaction of dinitrogen tetroxide (N₂O₄) to nitrogen dioxide (NO₂),
N2O4(g) -> 2 NO2(g)
the system is at an initial temperature of 300.0 K under a total equilibrium pressure of 2.0 atm with K_p = 0.16. Upon heating to a temperature of 350.0 K, the equilibrium constant K becomes 2.12. The standard entropy change for the reaction is 175.0 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.

Assuming the standard enthalpy change and standard entropy change are temperature-independent over this range, calculate the temperature at which ΔG = 0.

(Given: R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; ln(13.25) = 2.584)

Give the answer in K, to 3 significant figures.

A sample of nitrogen dioxide (NO₂) collected over water (H₂O) at 25 °C exerts a total pressure of 0.672 atm. The gas is transferred into an evacuated chamber containing activated charcoal (C) and allowed to reach adsorption equilibrium at the same temperature. For this adsorption system, the Freundlich parameters are k = 2.45 and n = 2.0, where pressure is expressed in atm. The vapour pressure of water (H₂O) at 25 °C is 0.032 atm. Calculate the extent of adsorption, x/m. Give the answer to 3 significant figures.

Methane (CH₄) gas collected over water (H₂O) at 29 °C registers a total pressure of 0.769 atm. The moist gas is brought into contact with hydrophobic activated charcoal, on which the adsorption of methane (CH₄) is described by Freundlich isotherm parameters k = 1.6 and n = 3.0 based on its equilibrium partial pressure. The vapour pressure of water (H₂O) at 29 °C is 0.04 atm. Calculate the extent of adsorption, x/m, of methane (CH₄) on the charcoal. Give the answer to 3 significant figures.

Activated carbon is equilibrated with ethane (C₂H₆) gas saturated with water vapour at 29 °C under a total pressure of 0.552 atm. The Freundlich adsorption parameters for ethane (C₂H₆) on this activated carbon at 29 °C are k = 3.75 and n = 1.5, with pressure expressed in atm. The vapour pressure of water at 29 °C is 0.04 atm. Neglecting the adsorption of water vapour, calculate the value of x/m for ethane (C₂H₆). Give the answer to 3 significant figures.

A sample of sulfur dioxide (SO₂) gas collected over water at 27 °C is allowed to reach adsorption equilibrium on activated charcoal inside a sealed container at a total pressure of 0.764 atm. For the adsorption process at this temperature, the Freundlich adsorption isotherm parameters are k = 2.8 and n = 3.0.

(Given: vapour pressure of water at 27 °C = 0.035 atm)

Calculate the value of x/m at equilibrium. Give the answer to 3 significant figures.

Phosphorus pentachloride (PCl₅) dissociates according to the reaction:
$$\text{PCl}_5(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3(\text{g}) + \text{Cl}_2(\text{g})$$
In an experiment at 450 K, phosphorus pentachloride (PCl₅) reaches equilibrium with a degree of dissociation of 0.45 under a total equilibrium pressure of 1.5 atm. At 600 K, the equilibrium constant for this dissociation is 12.0. The standard entropy change for the reaction over this temperature range is 145.0 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.

Calculate the temperature at which $\Delta G^\circ = 0$.
(Given: $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$)

Give the answer in K, to 3 significant figures.

An aqueous solution of dichloroacetic acid (CHCl₂COOH) has a concentration of 0.08 mol L⁻¹. Dichloroacetic acid undergoes dissociation into 2 ions in water, with an acid dissociation constant (Kₐ) of 0.05. Calculate the van 't Hoff factor of the acid in this solution. Give the answer to 3 significant figures.

A radioactive decay series starts from a uranium (U) nuclide with atomic number 92 and mass number 238, terminating at a stable lead (Pb) isotope. This identical lead isotope is formed when a parent bismuth (Bi) nuclide of atomic number 83 and mass number 206 undergoes positron emission. Calculate the total number of β particles emitted during the complete disintegration of one nucleus of the starting uranium isotope into this lead isotope. Give the answer as an integer.

Americium (Am) with atomic number 95 and mass number 241 undergoes a radioactive decay series consisting solely of $\alpha$ and $\beta^-$ emissions to form a stable nuclide. This stable nuclide is identical to the daughter nuclide formed when a parent nuclide of polonium (Po) with atomic number 84 and mass number 209 undergoes a single positron emission. Calculate the total number of $\beta^-$ particles emitted in the decay series of one nucleus of americium-241 to this stable nuclide. Give the answer as an integer.

The radioactive decay series originating from uranium ($^{235}_{92}\text{U}$) terminates at a stable isotope of lead (Pb) through successive $\alpha$ and $\beta^-$ emissions. This exact lead isotope is also produced as the daughter product when bismuth ($^{207}_{83}\text{Bi}$) undergoes a single positron ($\beta^+$) decay. Determine the total number of $\beta^-$ particles emitted during the complete disintegration of one $^{235}_{92}\text{U}$ nucleus into this stable lead nuclide.
Give the answer as an integer.

A 50.0 mL stock solution of 0.15 M potassium iodate (KIO₃) is diluted by adding 200.0 mL of water. A 100.0 mL aliquot of this diluted KIO₃ solution is treated with excess potassium iodide (KI) in an acidic medium and mixed with an impure 0.80 g sample of a reducing agent (equivalent mass = 50.0 g eq⁻¹). The unreacted iodate requires 30.0 mL of a 0.100 N standard reducing agent for complete back-titration. In a separate gas-phase equilibrium reaction, the equilibrium constant is K with ln K = 6.7657. The standard Gibbs energy change (ΔG°) of this reaction is related to the percentage purity P of the sample and the number of peaks N in the radial distribution curve (4πr²R²) of a 4p electron by ΔG° = −(P × N × 100) J mol⁻¹. Calculate the temperature T (in K) of the equilibrium reaction. (Given: R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; in acidic medium with excess I⁻, IO₃⁻ is reduced to I₂). Give the answer in K, to 3 significant figures.

An electrolytic cell operating at a constant potential difference of 2.50 V is used to produce 0.100 mol of hydrogen gas (H₂) by the electrolysis of an aqueous acid solution. The generated hydrogen gas is collected over water at 300 K under a total pressure of 1.040 atm. The dry gas is then separated and subjected to a reversible isothermal expansion at 300 K until the heat absorbed during the expansion (TΔS) equals exactly 1.20% of the total electrical energy consumed during the electrolysis. Assuming ideal gas behavior, the final volume of the hydrogen gas (in L) is ______.
